headline.title: First flakes for Adirondacks.
headline.text: Up to {{s:1.6}} on the summit of Whiteface early Friday to Friday evening. 29 of 31 resorts get cold enough nights for snow guns this week, mostly in White Mountains and Northern Vermont. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
After a quiet day today, a storm system brings gusty winds, rain, and mountain snow Friday through Saturday.
Temperatures trend near to below normal Sunday night through Thursday with mostly dry conditions prevailing.

ALY.excerpt:
) Strong cold front will bring gusty winds, showers and a few thunderstorms to the region for Friday, followed by blustery and unseasonably chilly conditions for Friday night into Saturday along with a few mountain snow showers.
) Dry weather with temperatures to near seasonable levels Sunday into early next week.

GYX.excerpt:
Low pressure crosses Friday through Friday night bringing beneficial rainfall.
Cold temperatures and strong winds arrive for Saturday, with winter-like wind chills. Moderating temperatures from Sunday into next week with rain-free conditions.

BUF.excerpt:
) Periods of rain tonight through Friday, along with gusty winds.
) Much colder Friday night through Saturday night with a few wet snowflakes possible early Saturday morning.

PHI.excerpt:
A cold front continues to sag south through the region early this morning. A warm front lifts north through the region tonight.
A strong cold frontal passage Friday evening will bring windy conditions, showers and potential for some thunderstorms, and colder temperatures into the weekend.
Widespread frost and freeze conditions are increasingly likely Saturday night.

RLX.excerpt:
) A stalled front parked over the area will gradually lift as a warm front today into tonight. Afternoon shower and storm chances will be primarily focused along the higher terrain by this evening.
) A strong cold front crosses on Friday, bringing showers, storms, and gusty winds along the mountains. A surge of arctic air infiltrating in the wake of the front will yield a chilly weekend, with frost and freeze conditions possible by Saturday night.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Just a coating for the high peaks.
paras: Light snow Friday morning to Friday night: Jay Peak {{s:0.9}} at the summits, though the models range from {{r:0.2,3.4}} at Jay Peak. Rain mixes in even up high at times.
Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:29}} to {{t:56}}, with up to {{s:0.9}} of snow and gusts near {{w:42}} up top.
Snowmaking: Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough for snow guns this week (46). Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8.
NWS Burlington forecasters: "After a quiet day today, a storm system brings gusty winds, rain, and mountain snow Friday through Saturday."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and near-normal precipitation.

insights.text: First flakes: about {{s:0.9}} at the summit Friday morning to Friday night (models {{r:0.2,3.4}}). It starts as rain ({{l:0.77}}), even at the summit, then changes to snow Friday night as colder air arrives. It won't last: highs reach {{t:49}} Monday.

Snow guns can run early Saturday to Sunday morning: about 34 hours cold enough at the summit, getting down to {{t:16}} once humidity is factored in. The base is cold enough for 14 of those hours. 1 more window follows this week.
Typically opens around Nov 27, 43 days out. Openings depend on snowmaking nights, not the calendar.
